atlas-ae.0128: Dubai Business Associates asks for fluent English, verbal and written, from a recent bachelor’s graduate; the selection stages are not published.
atlas-ae.0129: PwC Middle East’s graduate programmes are described in English; no language certificate is asked on the pages read.
atlas-ae.0130: English is the language of the banks and funds at the financial centres; Arabic matters for the national schemes and government-facing roles, which are for Emiratis in any case.
atlas-ae.0131: Employment contracts and offers are issued in Arabic and English, and English is the working language of the multinationals.
atlas-ae.0132: In SkillDrift’s analysis of 7,025 UAE postings, English was named in 21.3% and Arabic in 7.4%, against 13.2% for Arabic in Saudi Arabia; the sample leans to operations, engineering, sales and hospitality, so read the shares as a minimum.
atlas-ae.0133: Technology firms in the free zones work in English; no certificate is normally requested and the level is judged at interview.
atlas-ae.0134: MBZUAI’s graduates move into AI engineer, research-associate and data-scientist roles at G42, ADNOC and DP World; the language of work is English.
atlas-ae.0135: The World Bank’s modelled ILO estimate puts unemployment at 2.2% of the labour force in 2025, and 6.5% for ages 15 to 24; it does not split nationals from expatriates.
atlas-ae.0136: The Federal Competitiveness and Statistics Centre reports unemployment of 1.9% in 2024 and youth unemployment, ages 15 to 24, of 5.2%; Khaleej Times (22 June 2026) quotes employers saying a degree alone no longer secures a first role and that internships, portfolios and certifications are the new minimum, without giving a UAE hiring figure.
atlas-ae.0137: No source read gives a return-offer or conversion rate for the open programmes, or a time to first job for foreign graduates.
atlas-ae.0142: The university, accredited by the Commission for Academic Accreditation, sponsors a one-year renewable visa; the medical and Emirates ID follow on arrival. Part-time work needs the university’s consent and a labour-ministry permit.
atlas-ae.0143: The European health card is worthless here: you need private insurance.
atlas-ae.0145: AED 2,500 to 4,500 a year, plus a deposit
atlas-ae.0147: No internship on a visa waiver. Resident students need a student training permit requested by the company; candidates from abroad need an entry permit for training sponsored by a university or company, for 60 to 180 days. In the DIFC, interns get a visitor pass of up to three months.
atlas-ae.0149: Job-seeker visa and graduate grace period
atlas-ae.0150: A job-seeker visit visa of 60, 90 or 120 days, with no sponsor, for graduates of the last two years from a top-500 university or people in skill levels 1 to 3. It does not allow work; once hired you change status without leaving.
atlas-ae.0151: Graduates of UAE universities get a 60-day grace period after the student visa is cancelled.
atlas-ae.0153: AED 200, 300 or 400, plus a refundable AED 1,025 deposit
atlas-ae.0155: The employer pays every hiring and visa cost by law. You can change status inside the country if you are already there legally. Degrees must go through consular legalisation (no apostille) and recognition, or you are graded as a non-graduate.
atlas-ae.0156: Mainland firms with 50 or more staff must hire Emiratis each year; the DIFC and ADGM free zones are exempt.
atlas-ae.0158: unemployment insurance AED 63 or 126 a year
atlas-ae.0159: Quit during probation without the notice required (14 days to leave, 30 to change employer) and you get a one-year labour ban.
atlas-ae.0161: Self-sponsored residence: Green for five years with a degree and a skilled job, Golden for ten years for skill levels 1 and 2. Golden holders can live abroad without losing the visa. Recent graduates of a world top-100 university with a high GPA can also get a Golden Visa.
atlas-ae.0167: A one-year renewable visa for people employed abroad or owning a company abroad, with six months of bank statements and UAE health insurance.
atlas-ae.0171: Unpaid thesis or research stays up to 90 days fit the EU visa waiver with a hosting agreement; longer stays need a visa from the host. MBZUAI funds every PhD in AI fully, with a monthly stipend.
atlas-ae.0172: Scientists recommended by the Emirates Scientists Council can get a ten-year Golden Visa.
atlas-ae.0173: The UAE has no working-holiday agreements; the job-seeker visa is the nearest alternative.
atlas-ae.0175: EU citizens get 90 days in any 180 free of charge, except the Irish, who get 30 days on arrival. Working is a crime.
atlas-ae.0177: British citizens get a free 30-day visa on arrival, extendable inside the country. Working is a crime.
atlas-ae.0178: The UAE is not in the apostille convention: degrees and other documents need the full four-step consular legalisation in your home country (about €300 to €600), then attestation by the UAE Foreign Ministry.
atlas-ae.0179: Register your yearly lease on Ejari in Dubai or Tawtheeq in Abu Dhabi, usually in your first month.
atlas-ae.0180: The employment entry permit lets you stay 60 days to complete the steps: your unified ID number (UID) is stamped at the border, then the medical fitness test (DHA in Dubai, SEHA in Abu Dhabi), biometrics for the Emirates ID at an ICP centre, and the digital residence visa. The plastic Emirates ID comes by courier.
atlas-ae.0181: Until the Emirates ID and residence visa are issued, do not leave the country: leaving cancels the process and the fees paid.
atlas-ae.0182: The Emirates ID number is your identifier for government services, bank and contracts.
atlas-ae.0183: Your employer must give you health insurance, compulsory in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and, since 2024, nationwide.
atlas-ae.0184: Open a resident current account once you have the Emirates ID; salaries are paid through the Wages Protection System.
atlas-ae.0185: Register for the compulsory unemployment insurance (ILOE) at iloe.ae within 120 days, or pay an automatic AED 400 fine; it costs AED 63 or 126 a year.
atlas-ae.0186: A residence visa lapses after more than 180 days abroad, except for Golden Visa holders.
atlas-ae.0187: Between entry and the residence visa you cannot leave the UAE: leaving cancels the process.
atlas-ae.0188: A “trial period” on a tourist visa is illegal work: fines of AED 100,000 to 1,000,000 for the employer, deportation and a ban for you.
atlas-ae.0189: Register for unemployment insurance within four months of starting, or pay an automatic AED 400 fine.
atlas-ae.0190: Italy lists the UAE as a tax haven: registering with AIRE is not enough, you must prove you really left Italy.
atlas-ae.0192: Moving between Dubai and the other emirates can create a duplicate ID record that blocks visas for days.
atlas-ae.0193: Banks often refuse the digital Emirates ID, so newcomers spend their first weeks in temporary housing.
atlas-ae.0194: Old healed TB scars mean a 6 to 8 week culture test, stuck in limbo.
atlas-ae.0195: Degree recognition through the higher-education ministry and DataFlow can take one to three months.
